summary: Record the first executable controller skeleton as a cross-cutting behavioral implementation change requiring full five-stage review before further implementation proceeds.
reason: Revision 7 completed a five-subpass bounded Adversarial sweep and found eight blocker groups across initialization review binding, required typed domain/evidence models, identity serialization and controller-derived ownership, workflow terminal rules, persistence readback/signature completeness, persistence retry/outcome representation, frozen error taxonomy names, and typed operation-result payloads. Revision 8 corrects the aggregate blocker set within the first code-bearing Slice-1 boundary and intentionally does not implement deferred controller operations, canonical derivation helpers, a concrete backend, SQLite, or the conformance harness. Because these corrections change domain, workflow, outcome, and persistence contracts, the full review reopens at Adversarial.

reasons: Revision-8 Adversarial should verify the aggregate eight-blocker correction with the same bounded multi-finding decomposition used to discover it, while keeping each execution unit small enough to avoid context degradation.
The corrected skeleton still spans several distinct failure surfaces that should be rechecked sequentially with durable handoffs under the existing SUBDIVIDED execution mechanism.

decision.assurance_boundary: Semantic judgment determines whether one pass is suitable and which bounded subpasses require isolation. Deterministic policy defaults to SEPARATED, converts declared isolation requirements into ISOLATED subpasses, and permits FUSED only through exact pre-existing VALIDATED capability permission. The gate and completion validator enforce the recorded plan but do not prove the semantic assessment itself was correct.

findings: BLOCKING: PassOccurrence permits status=FAILED with a non-null semantic_result_id. The frozen Slice-1 model states semantic_result_id is absent until completed; the constructor only forbids semantic_result_id for OPEN and requires it for COMPLETED, leaving FAILED able to carry completion-only semantic-result identity material.

SUPPORTED: No additional runtime type/container/enum/boolean construction defect was found in the revised StateSnapshot, SemanticResult, CompletionEvidence, InitializationRecord, WorkflowDefinition/TerminalRules, typed operation payloads, OperationResult, InitializationCommit/TransitionCommit, or persistence result DTO constructors within this bounded scope.
unresolved_conditions: Carry this blocker through the remaining declared revision-8 Adversarial subpasses; do not stop the stage investigation solely because it was found.

Before a corrective revision can pass Adversarial, PassOccurrence must enforce the frozen semantic_result_id/status invariant for FAILED as well as OPEN and COMPLETED, with focused regression coverage.

findings: BLOCKING: OperationResult does not enforce review identity coherence with typed payloads that carry review_id. A well-typed envelope can set review_id=ReviewId('review:A') while InitializationData or StatusData carries ReviewId('review:B'), allowing one result object to assert two different review authorities.

BLOCKING: OperationResult does not bind OutcomeCode to the corresponding operation-specific payload type. Any accepted typed payload can accompany any success outcome, so combinations such as outcome=STATUS with RepairData or outcome=PASS_OPENED with StatusData are constructible despite the frozen operation-specific result boundary.

SUPPORTED: InitializationCommit and TransitionCommit internally bind their ReviewId to their StateSnapshot ReviewId, WorkflowDefinition binds initial_stage to the first ordered stage, and no additional contradictory well-typed combination was found in the bounded domain/workflow/persistence DTO surface.
unresolved_conditions: Carry the runtime-construction blocker and both result-envelope coherence blockers through the remaining declared revision-8 Adversarial subpasses; do not begin correction until the full stage sweep is complete.

Before a corrective revision can pass Adversarial, OperationResult must mechanically reject disagreement between envelope and payload review identity and reject outcome/payload combinations that do not belong to the same operation contract.

findings: BLOCKING: The frozen Slice-1 typed request layer is absent. InitializeReviewRequest, BeginPassRequest, CompletePassRequest, and RepairRequest are specified as typed domain request envelopes that separate caller-supplied expectations from controller-owned state, and Issue #11 implementation ordering explicitly begins with typed domain/request/result/error structures. The current first-code-bearing skeleton defines no corresponding request dataclasses.

BLOCKING: The revision-8 controller-derived identity ownership correction is not mechanically authoritative. OccurrenceId, GateId, SemanticResultId, and AuditEventId reject their direct constructor, but expose public derived(value) and from_string(value) factories that any ordinary caller can invoke. Those caller-mintable values can then be placed in typed payload/evidence structures, so the frozen requirement that ordinary callers cannot fabricate controller-owned derived identities remains unenforced by the API boundary.

SUPPORTED: The revision-7 missing minimum evidence models (PassOccurrence, SemanticResult, CompletionEvidence, InitializationRecord), explicit WorkflowDefinition terminal rules, stable required error classes, typed operation-result payload classes, and persistence readback/review-binding signatures are now represented in the revision-8 skeleton.

SUPPORTED/DEFERRED: Controller operations, pure transition planning, canonical identity derivation algorithms, concrete MemoryBackend behavior, SQLite, and the conformance harness are not counted as blockers in this first-code-bearing boundary beyond the typed request/identity contracts above.

Before a corrective revision can pass Adversarial, add the four typed request envelopes with runtime validation while keeping caller expectations separate from controller-derived state, and replace the publicly caller-mintable derived-ID factories with a boundary that ordinary operation callers cannot invoke as trusted controller authority.

findings: BLOCKING: The persistence DTOs do not mechanically guarantee immutable history/evidence content. AuthoritativeRecord.immutable_history, InitializationCommit.immutable_events, TransitionCommit.immutable_events, and TransitionCommit.immutable_evidence are tuple[object, ...] and validate only the outer tuple, so mutable dict/list/custom-object members can be changed after construction while the frozen dataclass still points at them. This violates the backend-neutral requirement that completed evidence/history be immutable and exact-retry/integrity decisions not depend on mutable aliased objects.

SUPPORTED: PersistenceOutcome now distinguishes created/already-exists, committed/already-applied/conflict, unavailable, and outcome-unknown states, and the protocol exposes read_occurrence/read_completion/read_initialization plus explicit review_id and expected_lineage_token on commit_transition. Those revision-7 retry/outcome omissions are therefore represented at the interface level.
evidence: Issue #11 Slice 1 persistence protocol and immutable evidence requirements
unresolved_conditions: Carry all prior revision-8 blockers plus this deep-immutability persistence blocker into the final integrated-adversarial-sweep; do not begin correction until that final declared subpass is durably complete.

Before a corrective revision can pass Adversarial, persistence-facing history/event/evidence DTO fields must be composed only of immutable typed values or defensively canonicalized/copied immutable representations so post-construction mutation cannot alter durable evidence semantics.
